title: Potinack
summary: Potinack is a Montauk placename for a hole or deep depression in the Hither Plains and Hither Woods landscape, with related watering-place references at Montauk and Amagansett.
listing_image_alt: Potinack, Napeague Bay archaeological landscape and corn fields
ancestral_territory_note: Shown in relation to Montaukett Ancestral Land on the current ancestral territory map.
why_this_matters: The Algonquian place name Potinack, designating a deep, water-filled depression in the hills near present-day Napeague, highlights how Indigenous terms functioned as highly specific ecological maps. Recognizing these traditional names allows modern park visitors to appreciate the deep, intimate knowledge Native peoples possessed about Long Island's unique geological features.
introduction_content: Potinack names a set of holes or depressions in the Montauk and Amagansett landscape, including a primary place near Hither Plains and the south-side cliffs.
history_content: Potinack belongs to the Hither Plains and Hither Woods topographic landscape on Montauk. Interpretation and earlier publication details appear in the historic moments below.
translation_content:
The name is interpreted as where the land sinks, gutting in, or where the land sinks or bulges in. The interpretation is uncertain because the form may instead relate to Appaquogue and flaggy land or lodge-covering materials.

Why Place Names Matter

“Geographical names play an important role in preserving, protecting and revitalizing Indigenous languages and cultures. Indigenous geographical names are highly descriptive, record detailed characteristics of places and features, and convey the intimate connections people have with the land and its resources.”

— Connie Wyatt Anderson, International Year of Indigenous Languages (2019), Chairperson's public statement
whereintheworld_content: Existing polygon geometry represents the Hither Hills / Hither Plains landscape imported from the earlier map. The exact Potinack hole, nearby flaggy hole, and Amagansett watering place each need local map review.
